originalTitle: US stock: S&P 500 ends lower as investors weigh data, Middle East tensions
simplifiedContent: The US stock market, specifically the S&P 500, went down after a period of going up. This happened because people who buy and sell stocks are worried about some recent numbers that show consumers aren't spending as much money as they used to. Some companies, like Applied Materials, had a bad day, which affected other similar companies. On the other hand, companies that deal with oil did well because oil prices are going up. Reddit's stock also did well after it was announced that it would be added to a important list of stocks, which made investors excited.

originalTitle: Nvidia’s $500 billion plan envelops Wall Street in its AI frenzy
simplifiedContent: Nvidia, a big tech company, has announced a huge plan worth $500 billion to help support companies that make artificial intelligence (AI) chips. The plan involves working with big banks to offer loans to startups that are working on AI technology. This is important because there is a high demand for powerful computing power to support the development of AI, and Nvidia's plan aims to help meet this demand. By providing financing options, Nvidia is trying to help the tech industry build the infrastructure it needs to support AI growth. This move is significant because it shows Nvidia's commitment to supporting the development of AI technology.

originalTitle: How a $900 million bet on SpaceX turned 100x into $94 billion for Alphabet
simplifiedContent: Alphabet, the company that owns Google, invested $900 million in SpaceX, a rocket company, a while back. This investment has grown dramatically and is now worth around $94 billion, which is about 100 times the original amount. This makes Alphabet the largest shareholder in SpaceX, meaning they own the most part of the company. Other early investors, such as Fidelity Investments and Saudi Arabia's investment fund, also have significant stakes in SpaceX. This matters because it shows how a smart investment can lead to huge returns, making Alphabet's early bet on SpaceX very profitable.

originalTitle: These 5 stocks are paying out more than their profits in dividends
simplifiedContent: There are five stocks that are giving their investors more money in dividends than they are actually making in profits. This means that these companies are paying out a lot of money to their investors, which can be a good sign that they are generating a lot of cash. However, investors should be cautious and check if these companies can keep paying out such high dividends without hurting their ability to grow in the future. This is important because if a company can't sustain its dividend payments, it may have to reduce or stop them, which could affect the investor's returns. Investors need to carefully evaluate these companies to make informed decisions.

originalTitle: Singapore Stocks’ Record Run Gets ‘Goldilocks’ Boost From Growth
simplifiedContent: Singapore's stock market has been doing very well lately, even better than the rest of the world. This is because the stocks in Singapore are strong in two main areas: they pay out a lot of dividends, and the companies have healthy financial situations. Recently, the economy has been "just right" for these stocks, which is sometimes called a "Goldilocks" situation. This combination of strengths has helped Singapore's stocks perform exceptionally well over the past month. As a result, investors in Singapore's stock market have seen their investments do better than those in other parts of the world.

originalTitle: Jane Street Lost $15 Billion in Its First Down Month in a Decade
simplifiedContent: Jane Street, a company that invests money, lost about $15 billion in July, which is a big deal because it's the first time they've lost money in a month in around 10 years. This happened because one of the investments they made, called Situational Awareness, didn't do well and affected the prices of stocks in the market. As a result, Jane Street's losses were significant. This matters because it shows that even experienced investors like Jane Street can have bad months, and it can impact the overall stock market. The loss is notable because of Jane Street's long streak of successful months, making this a rare and significant event.
